sector: Private education: lessons, nursery, primary, secondary, boarding and university
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: Parents or sponsors pay tuition per term (three a year in Nigeria) or per semester at university, plus add-ons for boarding, meals, transport and exam registration. Exam fees pass straight to the exam body. The biggest cost is teacher pay, paid every month including holidays, then buildings, power and food. Profit comes from keeping classrooms full up to the safe class size, keeping good teachers, and earning results that build reputation and waiting lists.

caseStudies.scale: FY2025 revenue guidance $2.37-2.385bn; 240,200 average enrolments in Q3 FY2025, revenue $2,415 per enrolment that quarter.
caseStudies.lesson: Revenue is fee per enrolment times enrolments, and teaching is about 60% of revenue. Copy: income scales with seats filled, while teacher cost scales with classes run.

caseStudies.scale: 2025 service revenue $1,106.1m; 136,239 partner enrolments at 31 Dec 2025; GAAP operating margin 24.0%.
caseStudies.lesson: A university grows by adding enrolments to programmes that are already accredited, and margins are steady once the accreditation is in place. Copy: the university licence comes first, then enrolment scales.

caseStudies.scale: 2026/27 fees for Nigerian students run from N1.71m to N4.64m a session (Medicine is the highest), with accommodation included.
caseStudies.lesson: Fee bands vary by faculty because lab-heavy courses cost more to run. Scholarships sit beside full fees. Copy: university price tiers by course, and a scholarship fund.

caseStudies.scale: Lagos day and boarding group; a third-party guide lists primary tuition at N8m-15m a year (2025-26, unverified estimate).
caseStudies.lesson: A premium Lagos group runs several campuses with a scholarship programme, and its results support premium fees. Copy: reputation unlocks higher fee tiers and new campuses.

regulation.unitedStates: State education departments set private school rules; most require registration or approval. Child-care centres need a state child-care licence.
regulation.nigeria: State ministry approval: in Lagos, the Office of Education Quality Assurance runs a form, evaluator visit, grading, invoice and approval letter.

regulation.unitedStates: State fire, building and child-care codes set capacity and adult ratios; private K-12 class size is mostly left to the school.
regulation.nigeria: Lagos guidelines: nursery max 25 at 1:8 adult ratio, primary up to 35 with 2 adults, at least 6 WC toilets, set plot sizes.

regulation.unitedStates: Voluntary K-12 accreditors such as Cognia review schools on standards and site visits; parents and colleges look for it.
regulation.nigeria: State ministry grading plus WAEC and NECO approval as an exam centre before candidates can sit exams on site.

regulation.unitedStates: Public and most charter teachers need state certification; private school rules vary by state.
regulation.nigeria: Teachers must hold recognised qualifications (TRCN registration); Lagos asks heads for a B.Ed or NCE and 10 years' experience.

regulation.unitedStates: State assessments for public and charter schools; private schools choose tests such as the SAT, run by College Board.
regulation.nigeria: WAEC (N27,000) and NECO (N22,250) set fees for 2026; a rise to N50,000 was suspended in July 2026.

regulation.unitedStates: State authorisation plus a federally recognised accreditor (GCU: Higher Learning Commission) before federal student aid can flow.
regulation.nigeria: National Universities Commission: N5m form and N25m processing fee (2025), site visits, then a provisional licence; 168 private of 309 universities.

gameRules.name: Enrolment at term start
gameRules.rule: Each term: seats = classrooms x cap. applicants = waitlist + round(freeSeats x reputation/100 x 1.2). Fill seats; extra go to waitlist (max 50% of seats). 1 in 20 seats is a free scholarship seat.
gameRules.playerFeels: Good results fill rooms and build a waiting list.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Stride and GCE revenue = enrolments x fee; Nigerian schools fill by word of mouth and waiting lists.

gameRules.name: Class size limits
gameRules.rule: Cap per class: nursery 25, primary 30, secondary 35, lecture hall 60. A class over cap cannot enrol. Each class needs 1 qualified teacher; nursery also needs 1 assistant per 25.
gameRules.playerFeels: I must build rooms and hire, not just cram desks.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Lagos nursery max 25 and primary up to 35 with 2 adults; US private ratio 9.8.

gameRules.name: Teacher hiring and quality
gameRules.rule: Hire: class teacher N90k/mo, science teacher N160k/mo. Quality 1-5 rises 1 level per 2 terms of paid training (N50k). Salary 1 month late: quality -1; 2 months late: 30% of teachers resign.
gameRules.playerFeels: Paying and training teachers is how results go up.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Teacher pay is the largest cost (about 40-60%); qualified teacher rules from state ministries.

gameRules.name: Term fee collection
gameRules.rule: 3 terms a year. At resumption 60% of fees arrive, 35% by mid-term, 5% never (3% with a bursar). Unpaid fees only cut cash: the pupil keeps learning and gets a polite reminder. Instalment plan: +5% enrolment.
gameRules.playerFeels: Cash comes in bursts and I must chase it kindly.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Nigerian schools bill per term and accept part payment at resumption.

gameRules.name: Holiday payroll reserve
gameRules.rule: Salaries are paid every month, fees only in term months. Warn when cash < 1 month payroll. Auto-save slider: put 0-50% of each fee burst into a payroll pot; 33% covers the 4 holiday months.
gameRules.playerFeels: I save in term time so no teacher is owed in August.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Term-based fees vs 12-month payroll in Nigerian private schools.

gameRules.name: Exam results drive reputation
gameRules.rule: passRate% = 35 + 10 x avg teacher quality + 10 if lab built, max 98. Reputation += (passRate - 60) / 4 each exam season. Exam fee N27,000 or N22,250 per candidate passes 100% to the exam body.
gameRules.playerFeels: Results day decides next year's enrolment.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: WAEC/NECO results are the main advert for Nigerian schools; exam fees are pass-through.

gameRules.name: Inspections
gameRules.rule: Each term 25% chance of a visit (100% before each new stage). Score = avg of toilets, fence, qualified teachers %, classes within cap, first aid. >=70 pass, +3 rep; 50-69 fix within 30 days; <50 enrolment frozen 1 term.
gameRules.playerFeels: Clean toilets and safe rooms matter as much as lessons.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Lagos evaluator visits and grading; Cognia site reviews in the US.

gameRules.name: Boarding care
gameRules.rule: Boarding needs 1 matron per 60 boarders, 1 nurse per 150 and 3 meals a day (N2,000 food cost per boarder per day). Any missed meal day: rep -2. No nurse: boarding intake closed.
gameRules.playerFeels: Boarders are in my care day and night.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Boarding fee add-ons of N450k-900k a term at mid-range schools pay for food and care staff.

stages.licenceOrGate: None: home lessons for up to 20 pupils

uniqueMechanics.name: Term calendar cash
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Watches three fee bursts and twelve paydays on a year calendar, sets how much of each burst goes to the payroll pot, and offers instalment plans.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Year calendar with term bands, payroll pot slider, bursar's fee ledger with paid, part-paid and reminder status.

uniqueMechanics.name: Classes and timetable
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Opens classes, assigns one teacher to each, watches class-size bars against the cap, and sends teachers to training to raise quality.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Class board: each class card shows pupils/cap, teacher, quality stars; hire and train buttons.

uniqueMechanics.name: Results day and inspections
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Prepares classrooms, toilets and first aid for visits, then sees exam results turn into reputation and next term's applicants.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Inspection checklist with score, results-day pop-up with pass rate and reputation change.

failureStates.consequence: 30% of teachers resign; their classes pause and pass rate falls
failureStates.recovery: Clear arrears from the payroll pot or a short bank loan, then rehire

failureStates.consequence: No new pupils for 1 term; current pupils keep learning
failureStates.recovery: Fix listed items and book a re-inspection after 30 days

failureStates.trigger: Pass rate below 40% for 2 exam seasons
failureStates.recovery: Hire subject teachers, fund training, equip the lab

failureStates.trigger: 3 missed meal days in a term or no nurse for 150 boarders
failureStates.recovery: Hire care staff, restock the dining hall, pass a boarding re-inspection

balanceNotes: Payback months by stage: 1) 4, 2) 10, 3) 19, 4) 21, 5) 22, 6) 21, 7) 56, 8) 55. Players will feel stuck at stage 3 (the bus and six rooms) and hard at stage 7, where the university licence is meant to be a long quest. Tune first: fee per pupil and class caps, then the payroll pot share. If the holiday months feel unfair, show the coming payroll on the calendar earlier rather than cutting salaries.
openQuestions: Is the scholarship share fixed at 1 seat in 20, or can the player raise it for extra reputation?
